routes.reason: New roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent, 'The arc-topology and descent for etale cohomology', 122 items. Accepted, and the case for it is as strong as it gets. A regular-expression sweep of every roadmap extract in the atlas for 'arc-topology', 'arc topology', 'v-topology', 'h-topology', 'arc-descent' and 'arc-sheaf' returns NOTHING AT ALL, so no layer anywhere plans this material: the arc-cover condition on rank <= 1 valuation rings, the identification of arc-covers with universally spectrally submersive maps, finitary v-sheaves and the ultraproduct argument, aic-v-excision, the Milnor-square characterisation, and the applications to etale cohomology, Picard and Brauer groups and the affinoid comparison. The id is free in the atlas and 'etale' is a galaxy id. What is more, FOUR other extractions - PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17, PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24, PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21 and PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24 - independently propose this same roadmap with the byte-identical id, title and area, and PAPER-SCHOLZE-26 routes items to it; so five papers coalesce on one design job, and this paper, which introduces the topology, is its natural home. The findings travel with the route: E3 in particular means the brief must state the affinoid vanishing theorem as Theorem 7.3 does, with the smooth case restricted to constant coefficients.

Source route into DiamondsAndVStacks D0, 8 items. Accepted. D0 is 'Spectral topology, ordinary sites, and size', which owns the spectral-space and site-size material the arc-topology needs: spectral spaces and spectral maps, the constructible topology, and the set-theoretic care that makes the v- and arc-sites legitimate. Putting these there rather than in the new roadmap is the right division, since the v-topology side of the story is already that roadmap's business.

Source route into LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.0, 6 items. Accepted. LD.0 is 'Languages and interpretations'. Section 3.2 of the paper runs an ultraproduct argument - Los's theorem, ultrafilters and the transfer of first-order properties to ultraproducts of valuation rings - and that is model theory, not algebraic geometry. Item 4 already credits mathlib's Ultrafilter and StoneCech for the carriers, so what goes to LD.0 is the transfer principle itself.

Source route into GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5, K.6, 3 items. Accepted. K.5 is 'Relative and nonunital theories' and K.6 'Nonconnective extension', which is exactly where the paper's K-theoretic applications belong: the excision and Milnor-square properties of nonconnective K-theory that the arc-descent criterion is applied to. The route does not ask that roadmap for arc-descent itself, only for the K-theory it consumes.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1321, 23 September 2026. Verdict: accept.

SOURCE. arXiv 1807.04725v4 was re-fetched and hashes to 4cdf5593...6620, the recorded PDF hash, byte for byte; 64 pages. The published Duke version is genuinely unavailable rather than merely unfetched: Unpaywall reports is_oa false for doi:10.1215/00127094-2020-0088 and lists no open location, which is an independent confirmation of the extraction's account, and arXiv's submission history ends at v4 of 14 December 2020, so no later version corrects these points. The extraction's decision to quote statement numbers from the source rather than page numbers from an unseen published text is the right one.

MISTAKES. All three findings were checked at their locators and all three are confirmed. E1 and E2 are settled decisively by the paper against itself: the statement Remark 3.31 calls 'Proposition 3.29' is headed 'Lemma 3.29' on the same page and is called that twice more in the intervening paragraphs, and the result the proof of Corollary 6.18 calls 'Proposition 6.4' is headed 'Theorem 6.4' and cited as such in the introduction. Both are wrong environment names on correct numbers.

E3 IS THE SUBSTANTIVE ONE and is correctly classified as reaching a stated result. Theorem 1.19 of the introduction, labelled as Theorem 7.3, asserts vanishing above degree d for an arbitrary ell-power torsion sheaf when 'A is smooth or ell is not the residue characteristic'. Theorem 7.3 carries no smoothness clause at all; the smooth case appears only in Remark 7.4(2), only for constant coefficients, and only as an adaptation that 'can be adapted to prove this statement', with the same remark closing that over p-adic fields 'the general case remains out of reach by our methods'. So the introduction claims for arbitrary sheaves what the body offers for constant ones, and offers as a sketch. The extraction states this as a gap in what is claimed rather than as a false statement, which is right, and its two remedies are both available.

ITEMS AND ROUTES. 146 items: 4 library, 3 planned, 139 missing, every missing item routed exactly once, all dependencies resolving. The twelve declarations behind the four library items were opened at the pinned commits and each says what its item claims, including the two least obvious, WithConstructibleTopology (the type synonym carrying the constructible topology) and plusPlusSheaf (sheafification into Sheaf J D). All eight stage ids cited by the routes and the planned items exist in the atlas index.

THE NEW ROADMAP IS AS WELL-FOUNDED AS ANY I HAVE REVIEWED. Nothing in the atlas mentions the arc-topology, the v-topology, the h-topology, arc-descent or arc-sheaves anywhere; the id is free; and five extractions - this one, BHATT-SCHOLZE-17, CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24, CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21 and GUO-REINECKE-24 - propose it with byte-identical id, title and area, so they coalesce on one design job rather than competing. The paper that introduces the topology is its natural home.
